intro: This is Rhodiapolis, an ancient city in Antalya province from the 3rd century BC. It was the city of Opramoas, Lycia's greatest benefactor, whose tomb carries one of the longest records of public giving to survive from antiquity.
history: This small city in Lycia's mountainous interior was the home of the benefactor Opramoas. In the second century AD, after earthquakes, he sent aid to twenty-eight Lycian cities. The inscription cut into the walls of his tomb lists every one of those gifts: generosity recorded in stone.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the tomb of Opramoas and the theatre, then the basilica and the baths.
facts: Did you know? The Opramoas inscription runs to seventy-one documents, and it is the most detailed source we have for how public giving worked in the Roman provinces. In the second century AD, after earthquakes, Opramoas sent aid to twenty-eight Lycian cities.
outro: This brings our tour of Rhodiapolis to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. A generous man is remembered here; be generous to his city in turn. Enjoy your visit.
